name: Brooklyn Bridge
hint: Ships need the whole river: hang the deck from cables slung between two tall towers, and pull the cables back to both banks.

history.name: Brooklyn Bridge
history.engineer: John A. Roebling, Washington Roebling, Emily Warren Roebling
facts: John Roebling died of tetanus after an accident at the start of work; when caisson disease left his son Washington bedridden, Emily Warren Roebling carried the engineering to the site.
Each of its four main cables holds 5,282 parallel galvanized steel wires, and diagonal stays fan out from the towers for extra stiffness.
In 1884 P. T. Barnum led 21 elephants, including Jumbo, across to prove it was safe.
history.why: The first steel-wire suspension bridge, and the longest suspension bridge in the world from 1883 until 1903.
